title: Local Euclidean coefficient test spaces
statement: Over $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field], let $m,q\geq0$ be integers and $V\subseteq\mathbf R^m$ open. Define $\mathscr D(V,\mathbf R^q)$ to be the real vector space of smooth functions $f:\mathbf R^m\to\mathbf R^q$ whose support $\overline{\{z:f(z)\ne0\}}$ is a compact subset of $V$. For each compact $K\subseteq V$, its fixed-support space $\mathscr D_K$ consists of the smooth functions zero outside $K$, with the topology induced by the maps $f\mapsto D^j f$ into bounded continuous $j$-multilinear-map-valued functions with their supremum norm, for $j\geq0$. Equip $\mathscr D(V,\mathbf R^q)$ with the finest locally convex real vector-space topology making every inclusion $\mathscr D_K\to\mathscr D(V,\mathbf R^q)$ continuous. Here locally convex means that zero has a basis of convex neighborhoods. These are coefficient tests; their density and bundle interpretation requires a specified chart and frame.
